name: MobileNavServerItem
description: The tab: the server's avatar and its name in `MobileNavLabel`, as children. A press opens the popover, and so does holding it for 500ms (the long press of raft-ui's menus). Lifting the finger after a hold never closes it: the click that ends the hold is not a press, whether the hold opened the popover or found it open. It is never `selected`: it holds no page.

name: MobileNavServerPopover
description: The root: owns the popover's open state, like `Popover` (`open`, `onOpenChange`).

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. - `unmount`: Ends the closing phase of the popover after an externally controlled closing animation finishes. Call `preventUnmountOnClose()` in `onOpenChange` first, otherwise the popover completes closing on its own. Whether it leaves the DOM is decided by `keepMounted` on the portal. - `close`: Closes the popover imperatively when called.

props.name: children
props.description: The content of the popover. This can be a regular React node or a render function that receives the `payload` of the active trigger.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the popover is initially open.

props.name: defaultTriggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the popover is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `defaultOpen` prop to create an initially open popover.

props.name: modal
props.description: Determines if the popover enters a modal state when open. - `true`: user interaction is limited to the popover: document page scroll is locked, and pointer interactions on outside elements are disabled. - `false`: user interaction with the rest of the document is allowed. - `'trap-focus'`: focus is trapped inside the popover, but document page scroll is not locked and pointer interactions outside of it remain enabled.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Event handler called when the popover is opened or closed.

props.name: onOpenChangeComplete
props.description: Event handler called after any animations complete when the popover is opened or closed.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the popover is currently open.

props.name: triggerId
props.description: ID of the trigger that the popover is associated with. This is useful in conjunction with the `open` prop to create a controlled popover. There's no need to specify this prop when the popover is uncontrolled (that is, when the `open` prop is not set).

name: MobileNavServerPopoverContent
description: The popover above the tab bar, 8px from each side of it and 8px above it, as tall as its content and at most 60% of the screen. The one exception: the list always keeps one whole server row, so where the parts after it leave less, the popover grows past 60% as far as that row needs (the floor, measured from its children into `--mobile-nav-server-popover-floor`). Where even that doesn't fit, the whole popover scrolls, the footer and the pages with it: the children sit in a ScrollArea (`data-slot="mobile-nav-server-popover-scroll"`) inside the popup. It stops below the top safe area (a notch in a standalone web app): Base UI's collision padding takes only pixels, so the height cap subtracts `env(safe-area-inset-top)`. The bottom needs none: the tab bar under the popover already pads the bottom safe area. A column: `MobileNavServerPopoverList` takes the room left and scrolls, and the destinations and the footer after it stay in view.

props.name: size
props.description: `item` for a popover about an app's item, such as the question before its link previews are shown: 400px, and `PopoverBody`, `PopoverTitle` and `PopoverActions` take a card's parts and 12px inset, like the item card (PreviewCard `size="item"`). Choose it by what the popover is about, not by its parts.

props.name: align
props.description: How to align the popup relative to the specified side.

props.name: alignOffset
props.description: Additional offset along the alignment axis in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the offset to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: anchor
props.type: Element | VirtualElement | RefObject<Element | null> | (() => Element | VirtualElement | null)
props.description: An element to position the popup against. By default, the popup will be positioned against the trigger.

props.name: arrowPadding
props.description: Minimum distance to maintain between the arrow and the edges of the popup.

props.name: collisionAvoidance
props.description: Determines how to handle collisions when positioning the popup.

props.name: collisionBoundary
props.description: An element or a rectangle that delimits the area that the popup is confined to.

props.name: collisionPadding
props.description: Additional space to maintain from the edge of the collision boundary.

props.name: disableAnchorTracking
props.description: Whether to disable the popup from tracking any layout shift of its positioning anchor.

props.name: finalFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((closeType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null)
props.description: Determines the element to focus when the popover is closed.

props.name: initialFocus
props.type: boolean | RefObject<HTMLElement | null> | ((openType: InteractionType) => void | boolean | HTMLElement | null)
props.description: Determines the element to focus when the popover is opened. By default, focus moves to the first tabbable element inside the popup, except when the popover is opened by touch — then the popup itself is focused to avoid opening the virtual keyboard.

props.name: positionMethod
props.description: Determines which CSS `position` property to use.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the anchor element to align the popup against. May automatically change to avoid collisions.

props.name: sideOffset
props.description: Distance between the anchor and the popup in pixels. Also accepts a function that returns the distance to read the dimensions of the anchor and positioner elements, along with its side and alignment.

props.name: sticky
props.description: Whether to maintain the popup in the viewport after the anchor element was scrolled out of view.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverList
description: The server list: takes the room left in the popover and scrolls inside it, a ScrollArea (a column with no gap, so its gutters move nothing). It is never shorter than one whole two-line row, and it opens scrolled to the current server's row (`aria-current="true"`), with no animation.

props.name: actionsRef
props.type: ((instance: ScrollAreaActions | null) => void | (() => void | { [UNDEFINED_VOID_ONLY]: never; }) | DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES[keyof DO_NOT_USE_OR_YOU_WILL_BE_FIRED_CALLBACK_REF_RETURN_VALUES]) | RefObject<ScrollAreaActions | null>
props.description: Methods to scroll from code that the container doesn't have natively.

props.name: children
props.description: The scrolling content, in ScrollArea's own container.

props.name: contentClassName
props.description: Class of a content element around `children`, inside the container: put padding and the content's own layout (grid, flex, `gap`, `stack-y-*`) here, so the scrollbars stay at the edges and the gutters layer is never one of the laid-out children. Only with it, `contentStyle` or `fade` is there one.

props.name: contentRef
props.description: An element whose size is the content's, watched for size changes (such as a hidden mirror of a textarea's text). Without it each element child of the container is watched, and children added or removed.

props.name: contentStyle
props.description: Style of the content element; renders it, as `contentClassName` does.

props.name: fade
props.description: Fade the content out toward an edge that has more past it. The scrollbars don't fade.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: How long the scrollbars stay after scrolling stops, in ms. At least 100 with `trigger="scroll"`.

props.name: onEdgeChange
props.description: Called when the area reaches or leaves an edge, and after mounting when the content overflows.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: The container's scroll events.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The directions the area scrolls in. Content too wide for a vertical area is cut off.

props.name: overscroll
props.description: What a scroll that reaches the end does: stop there with no bounce (`none`, the default), stop there but let Mac trackpads and iOS bounce the area (`contain`), or carry on to the page behind (`auto`, which leaves the container's own `overscroll-behavior` alone). Only in the directions the area overflows right now.

props.name: railInset
props.description: Room in px the scrollbars keep clear at each end, such as a sticky header's height, so they don't run over it. Also settable in CSS, on the root: `--r-scroll-area-rail-inset-{top,bottom,left,right}`, which don't inherit.

props.name: render
props.description: Another element in place of ScrollArea's own `<div>`, as the container (an element or a function that gets the props). It must hold children: the gutters are its first child.

props.name: size
props.description: Thumb thickness: `small` is 5px, `medium` 7px; both grow while pointed at or dragged.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description: The container's: by default `0` while there is something to scroll.

props.name: trigger
props.description: When the scrollbars show. They always show while scrolling or dragging.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverGroup
description: Rows that always stay in view, such as the footer actions.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverRow
description: One row at the option height of every popup list (`py-option-inset`, 36px for one line; a second line adds its own height and nothing else): a 20px avatar or a 16px icon, `MobileNavServerPopoverRowLabel` (or a `MobileNavServerPopoverRowBody` with a description under the label), then anything trailing (a check, a count), centered on the row. `aria-current="true"` marks the current server in bold.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverRowBody
description: The text of a two-line row: `MobileNavServerPopoverRowLabel`, then `MobileNavServerPopoverRowDescription` under it. The second line adds its own height and nothing else; the avatar and the trailing check or count center on both lines.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverRowDescription
description: A row's second line, such as a server's address: muted Space Mono; truncates.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverRowLabel
description: A row's label: takes the room and truncates.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverDestinations
description: The server's own pages in equal cells; a `group`, named with `aria-label`. Up to 4 sit side by side in one row (`data-layout="row"`). More than 4 take 3 columns, rows of 3 with the last row starting at the left (`data-layout="grid"`), so each label keeps a third of the popover and stays whole in every language. The count is of the element children, taken in React, looking inside fragments (a product puts the pages a guest lacks in one): counting them in CSS would take a structural pseudo-class on the children, which the WebKit selector rules in CLAUDE.md forbid.

name: MobileNavServerPopoverDestination
description: One of the server's pages: a 20px icon over a short label in a `span`, which truncates. Something new on that page (a feedback reply, a computer that needs attention) is an `accent` `Status` child, the attention dot at the icon's top-right corner: the server tab's avatar never carries it.
